  - text: CLASS 10 · CIRCLE PROOFS
  - heading "Angle Subtended by an Arc" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Compare the angle subtended by the same arc at the centre and on the circle.
  - text: "24 min Class 10 Circle Proofs Difficulty NCERT: Ex. 10.2"
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - complementary:
      - heading "INTERACT" [level=2]
      - text: Fixed arc AB
      - paragraph: A ● B ●
      - text: Drag point C on the major arc. Drag C around
      - slider "Point C around major arc": "0.5"
      - strong: C (x,y) (0, 1)
      - text: Measure angles
      - checkbox "Central angle ∠AOB" [checked]
      - text: Central angle ∠AOB
      - checkbox "Inscribed angle ∠ACB" [checked]
      - text: Inscribed angle ∠ACB
      - heading "LIVE RESULT" [level=3]
      - strong: ∠AOB = 118.4°
      - strong: ∠ACB = 59.2°
      - separator
      - paragraph: "Ratio 118.4/59.2 = 2.00 : 1"
      - emphasis:
        - img
        - text: Invariant confirmed
    - article:
      - button "Reset diagram":
        - img
        - text: Reset diagram
      - img "Draggable central and inscribed angle circle": Chord Tangent Angle 118.4° 59.2° O A B C
      - article:
        - paragraph: — Radii OA, OB
        - paragraph: — Arc AB (fixed)
        - paragraph: — Chords CA, CB
      - article:
        - text: As C moves on the major arc, the ratio
        - strong: ∠AOB / ∠ACB
        - text: "remains 2 : 1."
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The central angle ∠AOB and the inscribed angle ∠ACB stand on the same arc AB.
      - paragraph: The central angle opens twice as wide as the angle at the circumference.
      - strong: "Key idea: Equal arcs subtend equal angles at the circumference."
    - article:
      - heading "THE RULE (THEOREM)" [level=2]
      - strong: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle subtended by the arc at any point on the remaining circle.
      - text: ∠AOB = 2 ∠ACB
    - article:
      - heading "MISCONCEPTION WARNING" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Point C must lie on the remaining (major) arc AB, not on the same minor arc.
      - paragraph: If C is on the minor arc AB, ∠ACB is the reflex counterpart and this form of the rule does not apply.
      - text: "✓ Correct: major arc ✕ Incorrect: same arc"
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If ∠AOB=120°, find ∠ACB.
      - list:
        - listitem: "Given: ∠AOB=120°"
        - listitem: "By the theorem: ∠AOB=2∠ACB"
        - listitem: ∠ACB=½×120°=60°
      - strong: "Answer: ∠ACB = 60°"
    - article:
      - 'heading "CHALLENGE: DRAG & OBSERVE" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: Drag point C along the major arc of AB and observe two positions.
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Position ∠AOB ∠ACB Ratio":
            - columnheader "Position"
            - columnheader "∠AOB"
            - columnheader "∠ACB"
            - columnheader "Ratio"
        - rowgroup:

            - cell "Position 1"

            - 'cell "2.00 : 1"'
          - 'row "Position 2 118.4° 59.2° 2.00 : 1"':
            - cell "Position 2"
            - cell "118.4°"
            - cell "59.2°"
            - 'cell "2.00 : 1"'
      - emphasis:
        - img
        - text: "The ratio remains 2 : 1 for all positions."
